testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

refuted.claim: A re-Pull of an `impl-<N>=PR#<M>` row that holds a Gate verdict (`reviewed=...`) or an open review launch (`review=member:...`) still stops at the row step with its claim standing, because carriedTokens() carries only settled member tokens and ledger.mjs refuses a rewrite that drops a Gate verdict or an open launch. The new references/pull.md paragraph says such re-Pulls work ('A row rewrite carries the row's settled member tokens — ... `=PR#<M>` — ... so no rewrite drops one').
refuted.evidence: In the copy I seeded the row `#12 impl-12=PR#9 → PR#9 · review=wf:a reviewed=abc1234:2/0/0:run-abc1234r` and ran pullThrough (PROBE1). Result: status 2, err 'pull: #12: ledger.mjs row failed (exit 2) / ledger: row #12: drops Gate verdict 'reviewed=abc1234:2/0/0:run-abc1234r' — a rewrite carries every Gate verdict exactly as the row holds it', claims 1, releases 0, stage 'row', member 'impl-12-b', row unchanged. PROBE7 with `review=member:review-pr-9`: status 2, 'this write removes open launch 'review=member:review-pr-9' from PR #9's rows — an open launch is never removed', claims 1, releases 0, stage 'row'. With pull.mjs reverse-applied to its pre-PR version, PROBE1 fails the same way (member impl-12), so the bug predates this PR. It is the ticket's own failure (a stop at the row step with the claim standing), now on a different token kind.
refuted.suggested_fix: Either carry Gate verdicts and review tokens too (every word gateVerdictRefusal and the open-launch rule protect, in row order), or check the rewrite with the ledger's refusal predicates (rowWriteRefusal/gateVerdictRefusal/settledMemberRefusal) in stage_claim and leave before claiming when the row cannot be rewritten. Separately, narrow the pull.md sentence so it promises nothing for rows that carry review tokens, and add a pull.test.mjs case for a reviewed `=PR#M` row.

refuted.claim: A Pull row rewrite silently drops a malformed settled member token such as `impl-12=bogus`, and the Pull exits 0. The PR's comment and docs say 'a rewrite drops none', but `carriedTokens` uses `isSettledToken`, which excludes tokens whose outcome is out of vocabulary.
refuted.evidence: Probe in the copy: seedLedger rows ["#12 impl-12=bogus · impl-12-b=released"], then the Pull through to dispatch. Output: STATUS 0, DISPATCH name impl-12-c, ROWS ["#12 impl-12-b=released · impl-12-c"]. The `impl-12=bogus` token vanished with no refusal or warning. A direct `ledger.mjs row 12 impl-12=bogus` is refused ("malformed member token 'impl-12=bogus'"), so this only happens on a hand-edited ledger, but the Pull then repairs it without saying so. The drop is also inconsistent with the PR's own priorUse, which counted `impl-12=bogus` as a settled use of impl-12 when choosing the name.
refuted.suggested_fix: In `carriedTokens`, or in stage_row/exclude, refuse (Refusal) when the row holds a member token with `error !== null`, as `ledger.mjs read`/dispatch do for a malformed Dispatched entry. Alternatively carry it through so `ledger.mjs row` raises its own malformed-token refusal.

votes.reason: Ran the snapshot's real `settledMemberTokens` (what `carriedTokens` at pull.mjs:239-242 calls, used at the row rewrite on line 1022) on 'impl-12=bogus · impl-12-b=released · impl-12-c'. It returned ['impl-12-b=released'], so the bogus token is dropped. The code at ledger-grammar.mjs:118-120 shows why: `isSettledToken` requires a non-null outcome, and a malformed token fails that. The comment at pull.mjs:1181 says 'a rewrite drops none', and this contradicts it. I did not run the full Pull-to-dispatch probe, and I did not build a measure-copy. I did not run ./agent-test, so there is no red/baseline line. The bash tool was broken by an extension error, so I used Python subprocess to run node. I did not build a copy or run the probe, so this rests on reading the source and the claim's own evidence. The drop itself is plausible: `carriedTokens` (pull.mjs:239) calls `settledMemberTokens`, which filters with `isSettledToken` (ledger-grammar.mjs:118). That function requires `error === null`, so an out-of-vocabulary outcome like `impl-12=bogus` is excluded and a rewrite omits it. But ledger-grammar.mjs documents this on `settledOnLedger`: 'Malformed tokens are the caller's to have refused: one here is read as nothing.' The claim itself concedes `ledger.mjs row` refuses such a token, so it only arises on a hand-edited ledger. That makes the drop a deliberate, documented contract rather than a silent regression. The evidence shows only that a rewrite drops a token the grammar already treats as nothing. It does not show a defect in the PR. The `priorUse` inconsistency is real but minor, and the claim's evidence doesn't show it causes a wrong outcome. I'm refuting because the evidence proves something weaker than 'a rewrite silently loses a valid settled token'. unverified.claim: settledMemberTokens() and memberTokens() tokenise the row text separately (`split(/\s+/).filter(isSettledToken)` against `.filter(Boolean).map(parseToken)`). The meaning of 'settled' (error null and outcome non-null) lives in isSettledToken, while settledOnLedger/priorUse use `t.outcome !== null` and ignore `error`, so a malformed outcome counts as settled in priorUse and not in settledMemberTokens.
unverified.evidence: Read lines 112-128 and 971-975. priorUse's `t.outcome !== null` does not check `t.error`, whereas isSettledToken requires `error === null`. The difference is presumably deliberate: a malformed token still marks the name as used, but is not required to be carried. Not executed, and no test was run against it.
unverified.suggested_fix: Add a one-line comment at priorUse saying a malformed outcome still burns the name, so the difference from isSettledToken reads as intended.
